headline: ICT prosecution to seize assets of Sheikh Hasina and others
summary: Proceeds from the sale of seized properties will be distributed among the families of those killed in the July Uprising, according to the Chief Prosecutor.
details: The prosecution at the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) is moving to enforce the confiscation of assets belonging to ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and other high-ranking figures.
Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam stated that the home ministry will be asked to arrange for the sale of these seized assets.
The proceeds from these sales will be distributed among the families of the 'July martyrs' who were killed during the uprising.
The prosecution noted that no appeal was filed on behalf of Sheikh Hasina within the 30-day legal limit, removing legal barriers to the enforcement of the verdict.
Seizure orders also cover the assets of Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and approximately 11 to 12 other identified individuals.
Under the International Crimes (Tribunals) Act, the government and the accused have 30 days to appeal; the prosecution maintains that the Limitation Act does not apply to this special law.
The tribunal's verdict specifies that 50 percent of the accused's property should be sold and the proceeds given to the families of the victims.
The home ministry is responsible for implementing these orders, potentially using the Public Demands Recovery Act or the Code of Criminal Procedure.
caption:
Assets of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina and other AL leaders will be seized and sold to compensate families of July Uprising victims.

The prosecution at the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) is moving to enforce the confiscation of assets belonging to ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and other high-ranking figures.

Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam stated that the home ministry will be asked to arrange for the sale of these seized assets.

The proceeds from these sales will be distributed among the families of the 'July martyrs' who were killed during the uprising.

The prosecution noted that no appeal was filed on behalf of Sheikh Hasina within the 30-day legal limit, removing legal barriers to the enforcement of the verdict.

Seizure orders also cover the assets of Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and approximately 11 to 12 other identified individuals.

Under the International Crimes (Tribunals) Act, the government and the accused have 30 days to appeal; the prosecution maintains that the Limitation Act does not apply to this special law.

The tribunal's verdict specifies that 50 percent of the accused's property should be sold and the proceeds given to the families of the victims.

The home ministry is responsible for implementing these orders, potentially using the Public Demands Recovery Act or the Code of Criminal Procedure.

headline_marked: 2,010 hospitalised as [[6 more die of dengue]] in 24 hours
headline: 2,010 hospitalised as 6 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The total death toll for the year has reached 439, with the Directorate General of Health Services reporting a surge in admissions across several divisions.
details: Another six people have died of dengue over the past 24 hours in Bangladesh, while 2,010 patients were hospitalised.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the latest deaths bring this year's total toll to 439, including 20 deaths in the first two days of November.
The mosquito-borne disease was particularly lethal in recent months, killing 174 people in October and 148 in September.
In the last 24 hours, 943 patients were admitted in the Dhaka Division alone, followed by 245 in Chattogram and 235 in Khulna.
Other admissions included 219 each in Barishal and Rajshahi, 65 in Rangpur, 60 in Mymensingh, and 24 in Sylhet.
A total of 140,909 patients have been admitted nationwide this year, with 134,594 discharged. Currently, 5,876 patients remain in hospitals.
The DGHS has tracked records since 2000, noting that 2023 was the worst year on record with 1,705 deaths and 321,179 hospitalisations.
Last year, dengue killed more than 400 people and caused over 102,000 infections.
